## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package members: registered primary plan, docs/plans/2026-09-09-release-model-source-consolidation.md. Other subjects are governing or feasibility basis, not additional Delivery package members.
- Upstream review ID: design-review-r4; approved direction is proposal-review-r4.
- Review ID and round: delivery-review-r1, round 1.
- Traceability result: sufficient allocation of REL-SR-01–24, scoped SYS-SR-02/04/06/07/08/09, DES-SR-13/18/19/21 and published-skill-first R7/R8 into M1–M4, TG-01–08 and TG-FINAL-01.
- Material findings: none.
- Correction targets: none.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful primary targeted persistence.
- Open blockers: none for Delivery.
- Immediate next stage: return to route for authorized work initialization and implementation; this reviewer does not change activity or work.
- Claim limitations: exact Delivery approval only. No implementation, configured remote protection, publication, customer installation, source retirement, successful release, final Code Review, Verify or PR readiness is established.

## Independence and current basis

Independent agent /root/independent_delivery_review did not author the proposal, Design package, plan, implementation or tests. The parent authored the submitted plan and governing engineering contributions; this agent inspected them without editing them. Actual contribution separation supports independence.

The entire registered plan was read. Its inspected identity is sha256:a9604c2e49e78193c40b538023af54b791623ae9ecb0cb56d551a1f07af87985. Separate full primary context selections for activity, plan, model, review, finding, blocker, applicability and evidence were complete. The four registered Design members are Release, System, Design and the scoped published-skill-first amendment. Proposal r4 and Design r4 are current and approved; all three prior Design findings are resolved by their reporter and no selected blocker is open. Fresh subject inspection confirms every one of Design r4's eighteen governing/contextual subjects remains byte-identical. Earlier stale rounds retain their original meanings and are not relied on as current approval.

Read Release's requirements, current representation/population rules, immutable-candidate realization, authority/evidence boundaries, acceptance scenarios and exact source/consumer map against the full plan. Read the current independent upstream judgments and relevant actual helper/workflow/build/validation consumers. Upstream semantic Design assessment is relied on for its unchanged package; this review independently judges implementation sequence, proof adequacy and feasibility of the allocation.

## Sequencing and product outcome

M1 constructs a complete immutable candidate before any new publication entrypoint relies on it. It couples profile/version resolution, generated ownership and timing composition to actual archives, bundled metadata/index, packed npm and outer evidence. C is sealed source and the declared build overlay is separately bound; no final package digest is inserted into its own bytes. Generated expectations remain distinct from actual passed checks. M1 remains unable to publish.

M2 depends on M1's independent assessment and implements candidate-bound authorization, execution, public observation and durable persistence while disconnected from an automatic hosted trigger. Safe external adapters make the real executor/persistence testable without using real publisher credentials. Duplicate, competing, partial and uncertain outcomes are explicit; report repair cannot confer publication authority.

M3 joins those reviewed boundaries into the actual workflow/operator path and reconciles the older tag trigger. It must prove one normal approval, unchanged approved bytes at publication, real required validation, public observation and evidence-ref reading without manual generated-data work. Missing environment protection, provider identity, credentials or other required setup fails closed. Setup configuration remains separate authority; a checked-in workflow is not a claim that the remote environment is configured. The plan does not accept disconnected helper success as the completed user outcome.

M4 waits for that complete path and its reviews before removing exactly the six selected sources and mapped architecture portions. It preserves operational/historical inputs and evaluates actual readers, current reliance and follow-up ownership. A new unmapped dependency returns to its owner rather than becoming a seventh deletion. Each milestone has a coherent rollback unit and independent review, followed by fresh final whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify after all corrections.

## Requirement and proof assessment

| Obligation/boundary | Allocated proof and judgment |
| --- | --- |
| REL-SR-01–07: eligibility, profile authority, preparation, preflight and literals | M1/TG-01–02 covers complete and unknown/unsupported inputs, absent version authority, unexpected C/overlay edits, generated ownership, repeat/interruption, cheap preflight constraints and literal detection. M3/TG-06 confirms these are reached from the actual entry path without another normal maintainer task. |
| REL-SR-08–09/23–24: actual candidate proof, identity and shared composition | M1/TG-02 requires archives before bundled metadata/index before packing and real packed-install proof. Wrong bundled digest despite valid outer evidence, post-pack substitution and generated-pass confusion have negative detection. M2/TG-03 binds the exact retained identity; M3/TG-06/TG-FINAL-01 execute the actual repository command composition rather than a dry-run or substitute-success validator. |
| REL-SR-10–17: publication authority, event facts, smoke, recovery, deferral and privacy | M2/TG-03–04 covers rejected/stale/mismatched authorization with no external writes, unchanged satisfactory rechecking, duplicates/competition, definite absence versus uncertain visibility, partial provider outcomes, failed public smoke and evidence-ref CAS conflict. Captured write counts and retained records observe prohibited side effects; secret/deferral checks preserve mandatory facts. M3 observes the real workflow binding and bypass prevention. |
| REL-SR-18–19: timing and representation compatibility | M1/TG-02 distinguishes absent timing, malformed emitted timing and missing mandatory correctness/event facts; the first is nonblocking, the second remains a diagnostic-format defect, and required facts still block. Unknown closed values and old special/history populations retain their protection. M2/TG-04 and M3/TG-06 check that logger failure cannot erase required outcome facts or recreate a publication gate from duration telemetry. |
| REL-SR-20–21 and scoped DES/System ownership | M4/TG-07–08 requires a complete usable replacement for each surviving clause/decision/acceptance responsibility, exact six-source removal, mixed architecture retention, historical-judgment separation, operational baseline preservation, current reader/link behavior and FU-013's remaining owners. A filename-only map or automatic archive is not an acceptable substitute. |
| REL-SR-22 and scoped System composition | M3/TG-05–06 and TG-FINAL-01 require the full automatic prepare/check/one-approval/publish/observe/report path using real validators and the current evidence-ref reader. The original user outcome remains a completion criterion, not merely future work after source consolidation. |

All eight Design dimensions have distinct allocated observations: input and format partitions in M1; lifecycle/generated-versus-observed facts in M1/M3; identity/permission in M2/M3; archive/package/consumer composition in M1/M3/M4; repeat/concurrency/uncertainty in M1/M2; failure/recovery and forbidden side effects in M2/M3; historical/population migration in M1/M4; and missing setup/remote evidence/timing in M1–M3. The selected integrated hazards retain complete-path observations rather than parser-only proof. No Cartesian case catalogue is required.

Test maintenance is bounded by actual protective value. Existing fixture families, literal baseline, source-matching rules and negative assertions remain unless their owner explicitly supersedes the behavior. Timing consequence changes are selected by the Design, not inferred from deleting a test. Test discovery must include nonzero cases for each allocated group; external services may be substituted, but policy, actual validators and evidence persistence may not be replaced by unconditional passes.

## Actual consumer and command feasibility

The inspected baseline supports the plan's identified gaps. release-verify.sh enumerates historical supported targets through v0.5.0 and currently regenerates archive output; the plan explicitly allocates supported-version/profile selection and sealed-output verification rather than claiming an unmodified v0.5.1 invocation passes. Its dry-run skips actual commands, so the plan correctly requires executing real protected checks for complete-path proof. Existing release_transaction workflow parity checks encode the two old verify invocations and trusted publication argument pattern; their consumers must change coherently with M3 rather than be treated as timeless literal oracles.

The current YAML has a tag-triggered GitHub release job followed by a separately checking npm job publishing a directory. M2/M3 explicitly replace directory repacking with retained-tarball publication and prevent a new candidate being published independently by that older route. These are required implementation/proof changes, not evidence that the desired workflow already exists.

The candidate command flags match actual entrypoints: validate-adapters supports --adapter-root and temporary --clean-install-smoke; validate-npm-package accepts --package-root and --tarball; validate-release-ci delegates to validate-release with its recorded-source mode. The plan requires adapting actual sealed-candidate/evidence-ref consumers and running direct tests when their boundary changes. Existing release tests already have explicit external-evidence fixtures and public-provider interfaces; those are a feasible basis for bounded substitutes. New full-path proof must extend the real suite, not reuse historical fixture success as candidate correctness.

The archive-to-bundled metadata/index dependency is allocated before npm pack, followed by the exact tarball's installer consumption; the older source-only local CLI fixture is explicitly excluded as a production candidate. Candidate metadata and dependent assertions have an affected/unaffected disposition requirement. Local/CI selection is inspected against actual changed paths and final immutable range; unselected required groups must run explicitly. This gives a reviewable proof path without requiring real publication or pretending that local tests configure hosted protection.

## Evidence and limitations

Actually performed: complete-plan read; bounded owning-model/source/consumer reads with cat/sed/rg; per-kind complete primary context; exact full subject inspection and comparison against Design r4; targeted review recording; scoped record-store validation and git diff --check after recording. The plan-authoring evidence records passing prose/readability/whitespace checks and 91 advisory readability warnings; those checks were inspected rather than treated as semantic proof.

No release regression suite, full verifier, package build, hosted workflow, remote configuration or public operation was executed by this review. All operational commands in the plan remain allocated future proof. Required fresh full-path and final-checkpoint obligations are not waived by this approval. Actual changed subjects/dependencies must be reassessed for evidence reuse after M4, and new contrary evidence must remain visible.
